bull_bear.body:
- 48-year heritage as an established Indian brand, with deep, long-standing supplier relationships supporting management of input-cost and geopolitical risk
- PAN-India presence enabling service of national fleet accounts and large fleet customers operating across geographies
- Deep channel relationships: a network of Indag Certified Retreaders and franchisee partners engaged through structured technical training, on-ground audits and faster information flow on raw material trends and pricing, improving partner economics and stickiness
- Multi-tier portfolio addressing customers across price segments - performance-seeking and value-seeking - rather than competing through tactical discounting
- Technical service depth and casing-management capability, which favour organised players as radial retreading grows more technically complex
- End-to-end retreading solution: allied products (cushion gum, solvent cement, envelopes) complement the core tread rubber business
- In-house R&D function developing high-performance and differentiated value products
- Long-standing relationships with STUs and a disciplined tender approach in a competitive, L1-driven public procurement segment
- Conservative balance sheet with comfortable liquidity, prudent treasury management and no significant external borrowings, giving flexibility to invest behind FY 2026-27 priorities
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Commodity / raw material price risk — Natural rubber, synthetic rubbers (PBR/SBR) and carbon black remain the dominant input cost variables and are subject to global supply and crude-linked price cycles. The escalation in West Asia in early 2026 further tightened global synthetic rubber and carbon black supply, with continued upside risk to crude flagged through FY 2026-27 and the rupee expected to depreciate to an average of around INR 94.5/USD over FY 2026-27 - both of which can pressure landed input costs. Managed through weekly price monitoring, calibrated pass-through and supplier diversification across geographies.
- Logistics, supply chain and geopolitical risk — Geopolitical events in early 2026 affected synthetic rubber and carbon black availability and freight economics. Approximately 40% of India's natural rubber consumption and close to half of the tyre industry's synthetic rubber requirement are met through imports, making global trade dynamics, anti-dumping actions and shifting tariff regimes directly relevant to input costs even though the direct impact on the retreading segment is limited. Managed through vendor diversification, inventory discipline and production-vs-indent planning.
- Demand and competitive intensity — The organised retreading market continues to see competitive activity from established players and new entrants. Volume risk is managed through the multi-tier premium/value portfolio, deep channel relationships and technical service, with management explicitly stating it meets competition with quality, consistency and partner economics rather than tactical discounting - implying margin exposure if it has to defend share on price.
- STU revenue concentration and public-procurement volatility — The State Transport Undertaking business is subject to the variable cadence of government procurement, with revenue concentration tied to highly competitive, L1-driven public tender awards - an inherently lumpy, price-competitive channel that the Company can lose on any single tender cycle.
- Radial casing quality and rejection rates — Casing rejection rates for radial tyres are materially higher than for bias tyres, reflecting the lower repair-tolerance of steel-belted radial construction, and remain elevated industry-wide. Because M&HCV radialisation has already crossed 60% and is trending to 68-70% by FY30, this is a structural constraint on retreadable casing supply and is described as a near-term headwind for the retreading industry.
- Subsidiary execution risk at Millenium — As Millenium scales from its first commercial order to volume production in power electronics for BESS, execution risks around supply chain, working capital and customer development are actively monitored, with progress reviewed regularly at Board level. The adjacency is early-stage and unproven at volume.
- Valuation of the investment in an oil exploration company in Nigeria (auditor Emphasis of Matter) — The auditors drew attention to Note 46 on the valuation of the Company's investment in an oil exploration company in Nigeria: the fair value is subject to the successful exploration and production of hydrocarbon from the mining asset, and the outcome cannot be determined at present because exploration and production is on hold due to restrictions on flaring of gas by the Nigerian government. The auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.
- Regulatory, compliance and interest-rate/treasury risk — EPR, GST and environmental regulations continue to evolve, requiring active monitoring and a structured compliance framework. Separately, treasury investments carry interest-rate and mark-to-market exposure, managed with a laddered maturity profile, conservative credit selection and avoidance of concentration in long-duration instruments. Management states that during the year no major risks were identified that, in the Board's opinion, threaten the existence of the Company.

business.body: Indag manufactures and sells tread rubber and allied retreading consumables used to retread commercial-vehicle tyres, positioning itself as an end-to-end products and solutions provider in the retreading segment. It goes to market principally through its network of Indag Certified Retreaders and franchisee partners, serving private fleet operators (the PVT segment, described as the largest contributor to revenue) and State Transport Undertakings, with a clear focus on national accounts and large fleet owners across geographies. A 51%-held subsidiary, Millenium Manufacturing Systems Pvt. Ltd., manufactures power electronics for the renewable energy and Battery Energy Storage System industries as a clean-energy adjacency to the core retreading business.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Retreading (core):** Indag-branded tread rubber, Premium / performance tier portfolio, Value-tier portfolio (launched in FY 2025-26)
- **Allied retreading products:** Cushion gum, Solvent cement, Envelopes
- **Subsidiary - Millenium Manufacturing Systems:** Power electronics for renewable energy and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Millenium Manufacturing Systems Private Limited — subsidiary: 51% shareholding per Form AOC-1; reporting period same as the Company (April 1 to March 31); manufactures power electronics for the renewable energy and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) industries; no dividend proposed. The Company has given a corporate guarantee to Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited on its behalf (approved by the Board on July 14, 2023, recurring), disclosed in Form AOC-2 as an arm's-length transaction not in the ordinary course of business.
- Elcom Systems Private Limited — related party: Entity in which KMPs have significant influence / control. The Company leases out its MRO facility at Bhiwadi, Rajasthan to it on an arm's-length basis for a term of 9 years and 6 months effective September 1, 2021, with the rent subject to an increase of 12% p.a. after every three years; approved by the Board on January 15, 2019.

outlook.body:
- Position the Company as an end-to-end retreading products and solutions provider, with a clear focus on national accounts and large fleet owners served off a PAN-India presence
- Anchor performance on the PVT (private fleet) segment - the largest contributor to revenue - by deepening franchisee-partner relationships with more frequent communication on raw material trends, technical support and product programmes
- Run a multi-tier product portfolio serving both performance-seeking and value-seeking customers, following the foundational launch of the value-tier portfolio in FY 2025-26
- Widen the value-added offering to the retreader ecosystem through allied products - cushion gum, solvent cement and envelopes - alongside the core tread rubber business
- Deepen digital engagement with Indag Certified Retreaders and franchisee partners through structured technical training, on-ground audits and faster information flow on raw material trends and pricing
- Engage proactively with STUs and OEM partners to position within the emerging Vehicle-as-a-Service model as State Transport Undertakings electrify and standardise bus fleet procurement
- Compete on product quality, technical service depth, channel relationships and partner economics rather than tactical discounting
- Focus R&D on high-performance products for performance-seeking customers and differentiated offerings for value-seeking customers
- Scale the Millenium power-electronics adjacency into the BESS / renewable-energy opportunity - volume ramp-up, customer development and product portfolio extension
- Continue to invest in product, channel and operational capability to participate in the multi-year structural tailwinds; and continue operational digitalisation of the control environment (HRMS, in-house automation)
- Manage input-cost volatility with well-tested levers: calibrated price pass-through, supplier diversification across geographies, and close engagement with franchisee partners
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report describes no new plant, line or capacity project for the core retreading business. The expansion narrative sits entirely with the 51%-held subsidiary Millenium Manufacturing Systems Pvt. Ltd., which manufactures power electronics for the renewable energy and Battery Energy Storage System industries. FY 2025-26 was a foundational year for Millenium: it progressed from factory homologation and product certification to securing its first commercial order, marking the transition from product development and validation to commercial revenue generation, and the parent supported it through a calibrated equity infusion to fund its green-energy and operational requirements during the year. Going forward Millenium plans to scale volumes meaningfully as additional orders are converted, leveraging its India-based manufacturing footprint; volume ramp-up, customer development and product portfolio extension are stated as the key priorities for FY 2026-27 and beyond, helped by the mandatory 20% domestic-content requirement introduced in December 2025 for VGF-supported BESS projects. For the parent, the stated intent is capability rather than capacity: to continue investing in product, channel and operational capability, and to invest behind the FY 2026-27 priorities of franchisee network deepening, operational digitalisation and the Millenium volume ramp-up - a balance sheet described as conservative, with comfortable liquidity, prudent treasury management and no significant external borrowings, provides that flexibility. Operational digitalisation delivered during the year included a new HRMS covering the employee life-cycle and in-house automation tools across reporting, reconciliations and operational MIS.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Replacement demand - the foundation of the retreading market - remains structurally resilient on an expanding commercial vehicle parc, longer freight movement and steady fleet utilisation; ICRA projects domestic tyre demand growth of 5-7% in FY 2026-27 with replacement the larger share of incremental growth
- Shift from unorganised to organised retreading: the organised segment is currently estimated at 50-55% and continues to gain share on GST compliance, radial technical complexity, and fleet quality/sustainability expectations
- Radialisation deepens: M&HCV radialisation has risen to over 60% (CRISIL) with a trajectory towards 68-70% by FY30 - structurally positive for organised retreaders with radial capability
- Offsetting headwind: casing rejection rates for radial tyres are materially higher than for bias tyres, reflecting the lower repair-tolerance of steel-belted radial construction
- Circular economy / EPR: retreading is increasingly a strategic ESG choice, with retreaded tyres delivering material savings of approximately 70% in natural resources versus a new tyre
- Widening cost-per-kilometre advantage of retreading versus new tyres as crude-linked inputs and fleet operating costs stay elevated
- Infrastructure-led freight growth: over 21,700 km of Bharatmala already constructed and Vision 2047 targeting 75,000 km of national highways; BMI forecasts India's transport infrastructure construction to grow 5.5% p.a. over 2026-2035, with the road sector at 6.3% p.a.; ICRA projects toll collection growth of 6-8% in FY 2026-27
- CV cycle stabilising: ICRA expects CV wholesale volumes to grow 4-6% in FY 2026-27 (M&HCV 5-7%, LCV 3-5%, buses 7-9%); CRISIL expects 5-6%
- Fleet operator expansion broadening the addressable market - organised logistics revenues projected to grow 8-10% in FY 2026-27 (ICRA), and BMI expects India's total trade to rise 5.2% in real terms in 2026
- Margin lever and risk: ICRA expects the Indian tyre industry's operating margin to moderate to 12-14% in FY 2026-27 from 13-15% in FY 2025-26, with crude upside risk and the rupee expected to depreciate to an average of around INR 94.5/USD over FY 2026-27
- FY 2025-26 profitability recovery was driven by tighter raw material discipline, an improved product and channel mix and the foundational launch of the value tier - management characterises the improvement as operational (cost, mix, execution) and therefore more durable than a cyclical tailwind
- BESS demand backdrop for the subsidiary: over 130 GWh of BESS tenders issued in CY2025 led by NTPC and SECI, a project pipeline of approximately 92 GWh at end-2025 (up from around 19 GWh a year earlier), and a mandatory 20% domestic-content requirement introduced in December 2025 for VGF-supported projects that favours India-based power-electronics manufacturers
- Structural drivers beyond FY 2026-27 - radialisation, organised-sector consolidation, EPR-led formalisation and infrastructure-led freight growth - stated as remaining firmly intact
- Millenium Manufacturing Systems progressed from factory homologation and product certification to securing its first commercial order during FY 2025-26, marking its transition from product development and validation to commercial revenue generation; further orders are expected to be converted going forward
- STU revenue is tied to highly competitive, L1-driven public tender awards, so order intake in that segment follows the variable cadence of government procurement

risks.note: Natural rubber, synthetic rubbers (PBR/SBR) and carbon black remain the dominant input cost variables and are subject to global supply and crude-linked price cycles. The escalation in West Asia in early 2026 further tightened global synthetic rubber and carbon black supply, with continued upside risk to crude flagged through FY 2026-27 and the rupee expected to depreciate to an average of around INR 94.5/USD over FY 2026-27 - both of which can pressure landed input costs. Managed through weekly price monitoring, calibrated pass-through and supplier diversification across geographies.

risks.risk: Logistics, supply chain and geopolitical risk
risks.note: Geopolitical events in early 2026 affected synthetic rubber and carbon black availability and freight economics. Approximately 40% of India's natural rubber consumption and close to half of the tyre industry's synthetic rubber requirement are met through imports, making global trade dynamics, anti-dumping actions and shifting tariff regimes directly relevant to input costs even though the direct impact on the retreading segment is limited. Managed through vendor diversification, inventory discipline and production-vs-indent planning.

The organised retreading market continues to see competitive activity from established players and new entrants. Volume risk is managed through the multi-tier premium/value portfolio, deep channel relationships and technical service, with management explicitly stating it meets competition with quality, consistency and partner economics rather than tactical discounting - implying margin exposure if it has to defend share on price.

risks.risk: STU revenue concentration and public-procurement volatility
risks.note: The State Transport Undertaking business is subject to the variable cadence of government procurement, with revenue concentration tied to highly competitive, L1-driven public tender awards - an inherently lumpy, price-competitive channel that the Company can lose on any single tender cycle.

risks.risk: Radial casing quality and rejection rates
risks.note: Casing rejection rates for radial tyres are materially higher than for bias tyres, reflecting the lower repair-tolerance of steel-belted radial construction, and remain elevated industry-wide. Because M&HCV radialisation has already crossed 60% and is trending to 68-70% by FY30, this is a structural constraint on retreadable casing supply and is described as a near-term headwind for the retreading industry.

As Millenium scales from its first commercial order to volume production in power electronics for BESS, execution risks around supply chain, working capital and customer development are actively monitored, with progress reviewed regularly at Board level. The adjacency is early-stage and unproven at volume.

risks.risk: Valuation of the investment in an oil exploration company in Nigeria (auditor Emphasis of Matter)
risks.note: The auditors drew attention to Note 46 on the valuation of the Company's investment in an oil exploration company in Nigeria: the fair value is subject to the successful exploration and production of hydrocarbon from the mining asset, and the outcome cannot be determined at present because exploration and production is on hold due to restrictions on flaring of gas by the Nigerian government. The auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.

EPR, GST and environmental regulations continue to evolve, requiring active monitoring and a structured compliance framework. Separately, treasury investments carry interest-rate and mark-to-market exposure, managed with a laddered maturity profile, conservative credit selection and avoidance of concentration in long-duration instruments. Management states that during the year no major risks were identified that, in the Board's opinion, threaten the existence of the Company.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Indag Rubber Limited is an organised Indian tyre-retreading company with a 48-year heritage as an established Indian brand, supplying Indag-branded tread rubber and allied retreading products PAN-India through a network of certified franchisee retreaders.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Indag manufactures and sells tread rubber and allied retreading consumables used to retread commercial-vehicle tyres, positioning itself as an end-to-end products and solutions provider in the retreading segment. It goes to market principally through its network of Indag Certified Retreaders and franchisee partners, serving private fleet operators (the PVT segment, described as the largest contributor to revenue) and State Transport Undertakings, with a clear focus on national accounts and large fleet owners across geographies. A 51%-held subsidiary, Millenium Manufacturing Systems Pvt. Ltd., manufactures power electronics for the renewable energy and Battery Energy Storage System industries as a clean-energy adjacency to the core retreading business.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Millenium Manufacturing Systems Private Limited — subsidiary: 51% shareholding per Form AOC-1; reporting period same as the Company (April 1 to March 31); manufactures power electronics for the renewable energy and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) industries; no dividend proposed. The Company has given a corporate guarantee to Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited on its behalf (approved by the Board on July 14, 2023, recurring), disclosed in Form AOC-2 as an arm's-length transaction not in the ordinary course of business.
- Elcom Systems Private Limited — related party: Entity in which KMPs have significant influence / control. The Company leases out its MRO facility at Bhiwadi, Rajasthan to it on an arm's-length basis for a term of 9 years and 6 months effective September 1, 2021, with the rent subject to an increase of 12% p.a. after every three years; approved by the Board on January 15, 2019.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Retreading (core):** Indag-branded tread rubber, Premium / performance tier portfolio, Value-tier portfolio (launched in FY 2025-26)
- **Allied retreading products:** Cushion gum, Solvent cement, Envelopes
- **Subsidiary - Millenium Manufacturing Systems:** Power electronics for renewable energy and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Private fleet operators (PVT segment) - largest contributor to revenue
- State Transport Undertakings (STU) - public bus fleets, won through L1-driven public tenders
- National accounts and large fleet owners operating across geographies
- Franchisee retreaders / Indag Certified Retreaders channel
- India (PAN-India presence)
- Renewable energy and BESS value chain (via subsidiary Millenium)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Replacement demand - the foundation of the retreading market - remains structurally resilient on an expanding commercial vehicle parc, longer freight movement and steady fleet utilisation; ICRA projects domestic tyre demand growth of 5-7% in FY 2026-27 with replacement the larger share of incremental growth
- Shift from unorganised to organised retreading: the organised segment is currently estimated at 50-55% and continues to gain share on GST compliance, radial technical complexity, and fleet quality/sustainability expectations
- Radialisation deepens: M&HCV radialisation has risen to over 60% (CRISIL) with a trajectory towards 68-70% by FY30 - structurally positive for organised retreaders with radial capability
- Offsetting headwind: casing rejection rates for radial tyres are materially higher than for bias tyres, reflecting the lower repair-tolerance of steel-belted radial construction
- Circular economy / EPR: retreading is increasingly a strategic ESG choice, with retreaded tyres delivering material savings of approximately 70% in natural resources versus a new tyre
- Widening cost-per-kilometre advantage of retreading versus new tyres as crude-linked inputs and fleet operating costs stay elevated
- Infrastructure-led freight growth: over 21,700 km of Bharatmala already constructed and Vision 2047 targeting 75,000 km of national highways; BMI forecasts India's transport infrastructure construction to grow 5.5% p.a. over 2026-2035, with the road sector at 6.3% p.a.; ICRA projects toll collection growth of 6-8% in FY 2026-27
- CV cycle stabilising: ICRA expects CV wholesale volumes to grow 4-6% in FY 2026-27 (M&HCV 5-7%, LCV 3-5%, buses 7-9%); CRISIL expects 5-6%
- Fleet operator expansion broadening the addressable market - organised logistics revenues projected to grow 8-10% in FY 2026-27 (ICRA), and BMI expects India's total trade to rise 5.2% in real terms in 2026
- Margin lever and risk: ICRA expects the Indian tyre industry's operating margin to moderate to 12-14% in FY 2026-27 from 13-15% in FY 2025-26, with crude upside risk and the rupee expected to depreciate to an average of around INR 94.5/USD over FY 2026-27
- FY 2025-26 profitability recovery was driven by tighter raw material discipline, an improved product and channel mix and the foundational launch of the value tier - management characterises the improvement as operational (cost, mix, execution) and therefore more durable than a cyclical tailwind
- BESS demand backdrop for the subsidiary: over 130 GWh of BESS tenders issued in CY2025 led by NTPC and SECI, a project pipeline of approximately 92 GWh at end-2025 (up from around 19 GWh a year earlier), and a mandatory 20% domestic-content requirement introduced in December 2025 for VGF-supported projects that favours India-based power-electronics manufacturers
- Structural drivers beyond FY 2026-27 - radialisation, organised-sector consolidation, EPR-led formalisation and infrastructure-led freight growth - stated as remaining firmly intact
- Millenium Manufacturing Systems progressed from factory homologation and product certification to securing its first commercial order during FY 2025-26, marking its transition from product development and validation to commercial revenue generation; further orders are expected to be converted going forward
- STU revenue is tied to highly competitive, L1-driven public tender awards, so order intake in that segment follows the variable cadence of government procurement

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Position the Company as an end-to-end retreading products and solutions provider, with a clear focus on national accounts and large fleet owners served off a PAN-India presence
- Anchor performance on the PVT (private fleet) segment - the largest contributor to revenue - by deepening franchisee-partner relationships with more frequent communication on raw material trends, technical support and product programmes
- Run a multi-tier product portfolio serving both performance-seeking and value-seeking customers, following the foundational launch of the value-tier portfolio in FY 2025-26
- Widen the value-added offering to the retreader ecosystem through allied products - cushion gum, solvent cement and envelopes - alongside the core tread rubber business
- Deepen digital engagement with Indag Certified Retreaders and franchisee partners through structured technical training, on-ground audits and faster information flow on raw material trends and pricing
- Engage proactively with STUs and OEM partners to position within the emerging Vehicle-as-a-Service model as State Transport Undertakings electrify and standardise bus fleet procurement
- Compete on product quality, technical service depth, channel relationships and partner economics rather than tactical discounting
- Focus R&D on high-performance products for performance-seeking customers and differentiated offerings for value-seeking customers
- Scale the Millenium power-electronics adjacency into the BESS / renewable-energy opportunity - volume ramp-up, customer development and product portfolio extension
- Continue to invest in product, channel and operational capability to participate in the multi-year structural tailwinds; and continue operational digitalisation of the control environment (HRMS, in-house automation)
- Manage input-cost volatility with well-tested levers: calibrated price pass-through, supplier diversification across geographies, and close engagement with franchisee partners

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report describes no new plant, line or capacity project for the core retreading business. The expansion narrative sits entirely with the 51%-held subsidiary Millenium Manufacturing Systems Pvt. Ltd., which manufactures power electronics for the renewable energy and Battery Energy Storage System industries. FY 2025-26 was a foundational year for Millenium: it progressed from factory homologation and product certification to securing its first commercial order, marking the transition from product development and validation to commercial revenue generation, and the parent supported it through a calibrated equity infusion to fund its green-energy and operational requirements during the year. Going forward Millenium plans to scale volumes meaningfully as additional orders are converted, leveraging its India-based manufacturing footprint; volume ramp-up, customer development and product portfolio extension are stated as the key priorities for FY 2026-27 and beyond, helped by the mandatory 20% domestic-content requirement introduced in December 2025 for VGF-supported BESS projects. For the parent, the stated intent is capability rather than capacity: to continue investing in product, channel and operational capability, and to invest behind the FY 2026-27 priorities of franchisee network deepening, operational digitalisation and the Millenium volume ramp-up - a balance sheet described as conservative, with comfortable liquidity, prudent treasury management and no significant external borrowings, provides that flexibility. Operational digitalisation delivered during the year included a new HRMS covering the employee life-cycle and in-house automation tools across reporting, reconciliations and operational MIS.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- 48-year heritage as an established Indian brand, with deep, long-standing supplier relationships supporting management of input-cost and geopolitical risk
- PAN-India presence enabling service of national fleet accounts and large fleet customers operating across geographies
- Deep channel relationships: a network of Indag Certified Retreaders and franchisee partners engaged through structured technical training, on-ground audits and faster information flow on raw material trends and pricing, improving partner economics and stickiness
- Multi-tier portfolio addressing customers across price segments - performance-seeking and value-seeking - rather than competing through tactical discounting
- Technical service depth and casing-management capability, which favour organised players as radial retreading grows more technically complex
- End-to-end retreading solution: allied products (cushion gum, solvent cement, envelopes) complement the core tread rubber business
- In-house R&D function developing high-performance and differentiated value products
- Long-standing relationships with STUs and a disciplined tender approach in a competitive, L1-driven public procurement segment
- Conservative balance sheet with comfortable liquidity, prudent treasury management and no significant external borrowings, giving flexibility to invest behind FY 2026-27 priorities
